title: ghantika io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension result
description: Vendored, in-repo pin (never an npm dependency - no io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks package exists to depend on) for the shape of every response ghantika's Tasks-extension adapter (src/tasksAdapter.ts) returns: a minted CreateTaskResult (from run() on a Tasks-capable connection), a tasks/get result, or the interim tasks/update / tasks/cancel result - all four share this one shape - plus the single fixed not-found shape returned when a taskId does not resolve to a live job. The extension identity and the four-value status enum are the load-bearing, digest-verified facts this schema pins; config/tasks-schema-digest.json records this file's SHA-256 so drift between the two is caught, not silently trusted (see scripts/check-sdk-exact-pin.mjs).

taskStatus.description: The closed status enum this adapter ever produces. Deliberately four values, not the five the (deprecated, 2025-11-25, no-SDK-runtime) upstream TaskStatus vocabulary carries: this adapter never produces 'input_required' (a job-backed task has no client-input step), so it is not pinned here - a narrower, honestly-reachable set rather than an unreachable value copied for parity. 'expired' is never a member: a task past its TTL is REMOVED (task_not_found on the next read), never transitioned into a fifth status - see watchStopped below for the SEPARATE, still-working-compatible concept of the wake accelerator itself stopping early.

taskOutputCounts.description: The backing job's real, ever-cumulative output volume (never decremented by retention eviction) - present once the task reaches a terminal status, so tasks/get's terminal snapshot carries real evidence of what the job produced rather than a canned empty result.

watchStopped.description: Present once this adapter's own output-driven notification WATCH (the wake accelerator - see notifications/tasks/status) has auto-stopped early - currently only ever for a sustained firehose rate. Never means the backing job stopped: the job stays alive and pollable via output/tail regardless, and status can still legitimately read 'working' while this is present. Absent for the ordinary lifetime of a task that never triggered it.

taskResult.description: A live snapshot of a task bound to a real backing job. taskId is always the job's own randomUUID() job_id (one handle namespace, no separate task table).

taskNotFound.description: The single fixed shape returned by tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel alike for a taskId that does not resolve to any job - identical across all three methods, never an arbitrary/varying shape.
